mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate trend signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 9.5% indicates a weak labor market that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 9.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a broad-based economic contraction in the housing sector and labor market, which triggers a negative sentiment shift in equity markets, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The negative correlation between the joint movement of HOUST and UNRATE (decline in HOUST and rise in UNRATE) and SPX 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-demand regime characterized by strong consumer spending (RSAFS above $350 billion), the S&P 500 tends to experience positive forward returns as corporate revenues and profit margins expand, leading to a 5-day positive return.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of periods when RSAFS exceeds $350 billion.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output and economic activity, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO has increased for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI index level above 220 (indicating elevated inflation) signals persistent inflationary pressures that prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 220.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-interest-rate regime (FEDFUNDS above 4.0%), the S&P 500 tends to experience negative forward returns due to higher borrowing costs and reduced corporate investment, leading to a 5-day negative return.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a monetary tightening cycle that is associated with economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with labor market stress
failure_condition: The negative correlation between the joint movement (FEDFUNDS rising and UNRATE rising) and SPX 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.
